standard_prerequisites.name: The hypothesis that the intersection of a submodule with the multiples of an element equals the multiples of the submodule is what makes the lifting argument for the quotients work
standard_prerequisites.use: Proves the first implication by an explicit lift constructed from the divisibility of the image of one.

standard_prerequisites.name: The canonical presentation of the module as the cokernel of the map from the direct sum over the pairs of an element and a map out of the corresponding quotient

core_obligations: Prove that the first condition implies the second for a short exact sequence satisfying the divisibility hypothesis: it suffices to lift maps out of each quotient of the ring by a principal ideal, and for a given map choose a lift of the image of one, use the hypothesis to write the multiple as a multiple of an element of the submodule and exhibit the lift (proof lines 37601-37607).

For the converse, index the pairs consisting of an element of the ring and a map from the corresponding quotient into the module, form the direct sum over these pairs, define the map to the module by evaluation and let the kernel be the submodule (proof lines 37610-37617).

Observe that the first condition follows once the displayed sequence is exact in the sense of the second condition, and verify the divisibility hypothesis: given an element of the kernel mapping to a multiple of a tuple, write the tuple with almost all coefficients zero, use the vanishing of the combination to find a pair with the same element and the value equal to the combination, and correct the tuple by that pair's class (proof lines 37618-37634).
Conclude that the module is a direct summand of a direct sum of quotients of the ring by principal ideals, which is the first condition (proof lines 37634-37635).
proof_roadmap: First implication by an explicit lift for the quotients using the divisibility hypothesis (proof lines 37601-37607).
Converse: build the canonical presentation from the pairs of an element and a map (proof lines 37610-37617).
Verify the divisibility hypothesis through the correction of the coefficient tuple and conclude (proof lines 37618-37634).
difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes the modules that are direct summands of direct sums of quotients of the ring by principal ideals as those for which maps out of the module lift along every short exact sequence whose submodule is divisible by every element in the strong sense that the intersection of the submodule with the multiples of an element equals the multiples of the submodule (statement lines 37585-37598). The first implication is an explicit lift obtained from that divisibility, while the converse builds the canonical presentation of the module as a cokernel indexed by the pairs of an element and a map out of the corresponding quotient, and then verifies the divisibility hypothesis by correcting a coefficient tuple using the vanishing of the combination (proof lines 37600-37635). The construction of the canonical presentation and the correction step are the substance of the argument.
